title: Jailed in Thomasville, Georgia
summary: A fight at a dance led to the band's arrest, extorted fines and threats; a station owner trusted him for gas to Macon.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: What about Thomasville? Do you mind talking about that?

No, no. The reason for that is I had Tom Johnson in the band from here. I just hired Tom and I had a boy named Buddy Collins, who was a singer. And he started a fight in the auditorium that night of free-for-all. And I was on the front door with the principal of the school, taking care of the business and the money. They hurdled a whole band off in a paddy wagon, two girls I had that were dancers, the James sisters. Put them all in there. Of course, a few of the fellas got away. Mickey and I think it was Kato and bass player, a couple of others. Tom Johnson was playing trumpet. Brought us all to jail, locked us up in the jail. Called me all kind of nigger, smart nigger from New York. Took all the money. And when I asked him about going to court, he said, well, I'm setting this fine where the judge is going to set it. He says, the only thing you can do is this. There's an interest in the outlet to this town. I want you to use both of them. So, the other guys were missing. I told them I would go with them and help them find them. He told them I was too damn smart. And he told the fellas I was too small and nigger to be in front of them. In front of the band. And another policeman would come up there and snap the six-hute in my face six times. So, you can imagine 19 people in a small room, say 12 maybe. About 12 was as big as it was. But there's always one good fella in the world. You can't classify all white people in the same category. By the same token, you can't classify all Negroes as bad. We stopped at a service station. We were going to Macon, Georgia. And I asked the guy about getting some gas. I said, I need at least 150 gallons of gas. I'm going to Macon, Georgia. I don't have any money. Will you trust me until I get to Macon? He said, yes, I will. He said, you fellas was in trouble last night. I said, yes. And I also need five gallons of oil because the old busboy was a lot of oil. Well, the guy was real nice. He filled up both of the tanks and gave me five gallons of oil. When I got to Macon, Georgia, I widened back his money.
The demand wasn't involved in the fight or anything?

No. Well, in a way they were. There was a fella that jumped up on a stand and he wanted to do something to Tom Johnson. And Tom Johnson folded his sack stand and he hit this fella in the head. But I think all this was put up by the police to do this. And even they told the principal of the school that he came to my defense. He said, well, this man wasn't even around. So they said, you mean to tell me that you're a nigga here that lives in Thomasville, Jordan. You're going to take up for these niggas that come from out of town. I said, well, we'll get you fired in the morning. So the poor fella had to back off. There was nothing he could do. He was the principal of the school. And they took every dime I had. And they even make the girls, I'd give them the girls some money to put up in there. Apparently he used to hide it. They had them take it out and give it all to them.
